test_title: PYST 73: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 30 Dec, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is an INCORRECT statement about the endoplasmic reticulum?

options.text: The endoplasmic reticulum helps in the transport of materials within the cell, especially between the cytoplasm and the nucleus.
The endoplasmic reticulum stores genetic material in it.
The rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER) has ribosomes attached to its surface, which help in protein synthesis.
The smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER) is involved in the synthesis of lipids (fat molecules).

solution:
The correct answer is __**The endoplasmic reticulum stores genetic material in it**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER)** serves as a channel for the **transport of materials**, especially proteins, between various regions of the **cytoplasm** or between the **cytoplasm** and the **nucleus**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Genetic material**, specifically **Deoxyribonucleic Acid (DNA)**, is stored within the **Nucleus** of the cell, not the **Endoplasmic Reticulum**. The ER is primarily involved in the **synthesis** and **transport** of molecules, while the nucleus acts as the control center containing hereditary information. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER)** is characterized by the presence of **ribosomes** attached to its outer surface. These ribosomes are the primary sites for **protein synthesis** within the cell. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• The **Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER)** lacks ribosomes and is responsible for the **synthesis of lipids**, including **fats**, **steroids**, and **phospholipids**. It also plays a role in **carbohydrate metabolism**. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• ***Hence, the incorrect statement (and the correct answer) is that the endoplasmic reticulum stores genetic material.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Structure of ER:** The **Endoplasmic Reticulum** was first observed by **Keith Porter**, **Albert Claude**, and **Ernest Fullam** in **1945**. It is a large network of membrane-bound **tubules** and **sheets** called **cisternae**.
 
• **Detoxification:** One of the crucial functions of the **Smooth ER** (SER) in the **liver cells** of **vertebrates** is **detoxifying** many poisons and **drugs**, making them water-soluble so they can be excreted from the body.
 
• **Membrane Biogenesis:** Some of the proteins and lipids synthesized by the ER help in building the **cell membrane**. This biological process is known as **membrane biogenesis**.
 
• **Calcium Storage:** In **muscle cells**, a specialized type of smooth ER called the **sarcoplasmic reticulum** stores **calcium ions**, which are essential for **muscle contraction**.
 
• **Protein Folding:** The **Rough ER** (RER) provides a surface where **proteins** are folded into their **three-dimensional structures**. Proteins that are improperly folded are usually retained or degraded.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Endoplasmic Reticulum** is absent in **prokaryotic cells** (like bacteria) and **mature mammalian red blood cells (RBCs)**.
 
• It accounts for more than **half of the total membrane** in many **eukaryotic cells**.
 
• The **lumen** of the ER is the internal space enclosed by the ER membrane, which is distinct from the surrounding **cytosol**.
